message.content:
{
  "screen_decision": "include",
  "screen_rationale": "The study quantifies the agreement between preclinical electrophysiology data (in vitro and in vivo) and clinical QT interval prolongation and torsade de pointes for a broad range of drugs, providing a measure of predictive value and safety margins.",
  "arm": "safety-pharmacology",
  "arm_evidence": "Objective: To attempt to determine the relative value of preclinical cardiac electrophysiology data (in vitro and in vivo) for predicting risk of torsade de pointes (TdP) in clinical use.",
  "therapeutic_areas": [
    "cardiovascular"
  ],
  "areas_evidence": "The study focuses on cardiac electrophysiology, QT interval prolongation, and torsade de pointes, which are all cardiovascular endpoints.",
  "model_type": "across-multiple-models",
  "model_evidence": "The study compares data from in vitro assays (hERG, APD90) with in vivo data in dogs, and then correlates these with human clinical outcomes.",
  "species": [
    "dog"
  ],
  "species_evidence": "Data on effects on QTc in animals (lowest published values for doses associated with 10–20% QTc prolongation in beagle dogs, or other species if dog data were unavailable).",
  "endpoint_class": "mixed",
  "endpoint_evidence": "The study compares preclinical electrophysiology data (hERG IC50, APD90, QTc in dogs) with clinical outcomes (QTc prolongation, TdP), which includes both biomarker-like measures (QTc) and hard clinical outcomes (TdP)."
}
